## Accepted partial results; general complexity unresolved

Target: 3000029 / AMR-029-0029, minimum edge deletion destroying generic local
rigidity in the Euclidean plane for finite simple rigid graphs on a fixed
vertex set. Abstract topological planarity is not assumed. No arbitrary-input
polynomial algorithm, valid hardness reduction, novelty or priority claim is made.

The complete analytic report preserves:
- Exact rank-budgeted clique-cover identity and maximal-rigid-component closure.
- Bounded-minimum-degree/nullity XP algorithms; topologically planar inputs are
  a polynomial special case only, not a resolution of the general question.
- K6 with the K3,3 basis: all fundamental cocircuits have size seven, while the
  true cut is four, disproving the one-arbitrary-basis shortcut only.
- Clique-inflated K2,q family with a unique t-cut, unbounded residual rigid-block
  count, a 2-vertex-connected residual and unbounded degree/ordinary-cut gap.
- K2 cut value one and the out-of-domain one-vertex no-feasible-deletion case.

Classical rank/component structure, Yu-Anderson's degree bound and Lee-Streinu's
rank oracle are credited. A narrow Servatius printed-condition caveat remains;
it does not infer author intent or assert a replacement theorem. Original target:
https://oldlemon.cs.elte.hu/egres/open/Destroying_rigidity .
Classical rank-cover context: https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.11636 .

For finite loopless acyclic directed multigraphs with prescribed convex sets,
terminalwise simultaneous independent paths, the stated local bipartite
matchings, and coherent independent prescribed-set out-arborescences are
equivalent if each different-root overlap has at most one directed
vertex-sequence path between any ordered pair after parallel arcs are
collapsed. Same-root overlaps are unrestricted.

their Theorem 5 algorithm removes singleton tasks, checks weak connectivity
of the remaining reachable root pools, and charges membership preprocessing.

## Accepted complete theorem

For every prime p, every field k of characteristic p, and every compact Lie
group G whose finite component group is not p-nilpotent, the canonical
k-cellularization map Gamma_k R -> R induces zero in every homotopy degree,
where R = C_*(Omega((BG)^p-completed); k). Target: 30006658 / OWR-14299915-021.
Completion precedes looping. No adjoint-orientability, nilpotent-action or
spectral-sequence-collapse assumption is imposed. This is zero on homotopy;
nullity of the morphism in the derived category is not asserted.

The complete analytic proof preserves the finite-ideal Hopf-module argument,
odd-characteristic bosonization and characteristic-two boundary, compact-proxy
factorization of individual homotopy classes, arbitrary-field scalar extension,
and the correct contrapositive of Ishiguro's necessary implication. No
coefficient-ring generalization is claimed. Aggregate finite checks support
conventions only and no omitted executable is needed by the proof.

The originating question is credited to J. P. C. Greenlees, Oberwolfach Report
9/2026, Question 2.2, printed p. 594: https://doi.org/10.4171/owr/2026/9 .
Compact proxy and Morita inputs are credited to Dwyer–Greenlees–Iyengar:
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.aim.2005.11.004 . The finite-ideal theorem is credited
to Lomp/Sweedler: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0307046 . The p-compactness
implication is credited to Ishiguro: https://doi.org/10.2140/gtm.2007.10.195 .
Greenlees's related finite-group and restricted compact-Lie results remain

## Accepted partial; universal per-set target unresolved

For a planar point set S in general position, let E(p) be the set of
original hull vertices whose removal makes interior point p extreme. Under
the explicit hypothesis that all these sets are nonempty, the complete
fixed-edge injection proves
ppt(S) >= (product over p of |E(p)|) t(S).
The inverse recovers both the input triangulation and witness choices.

A six-point coordinate wheel has no contained pointed pseudotriangulation.
It refutes universal containment-only maps and Hall arguments on that
relation. It does not refute the requested counting inequality: the audit
independently proves t=11 and ppt=25 analytically.
The one-interior fiber identity and general weighted-refinement identity
remain in full. The necessary global compensation inequality is unproved.

Known results are credited precisely: the survey characterization and
Streinu attribution; Aichholzer–Orden–Santos–Speckmann family results;
Randall–Rote–Santos–Snoeyink's Catalan wheel difference; and the prior
containment obstruction recorded by TOPP 50 and O'Rourke's 2002 column.

P^3, quartics in P(1,1,1,2), and sextics in P(1,1,2,3). Polynomial degree is

extension and preservation of any projection pencil remain unproved. The

## Accepted partial theorem; original question remains open

For every k>=2, an explicit polynomial-size finite simple directed graph
with k distinct ordered terminals and unit edge costs has integral optimum
C_k-k^2 and an original edge path-distance LP vector of cost C_k/3, where
C_k = sum_{l=1}^k (k-l+1) floor(k/l). The lower bounds 3(1-k^2/C_k)
tend to 3; the actual gaps have liminf at least 3. Convergence of the actual
gaps to 3, exact LP optima, unbounded gaps and a universal constant upper bound
are not proved. The original constant-versus-unbounded question remains OPEN.

The full proof and mathematical audit preserve the characterization of every
retained interval family, the exact auxiliary optimum, internal terminal visits,
all arbitrary final edge cuts, finite protected bundles, LP feasibility,
harmonic asymptotics and polynomial size. No new mathematics is introduced
by this edition. A prior packaging-only checker correction was authored by
the independent audit, not the original proof author; mathematical proof,
source records and mathematical certificates were unchanged.

https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/46772

above and 2(1-1/k) below; the tight sqrt(2) result concerns three terminals:

For arbitrary real polynomials p,q, if p^(2i+1) and q^(2j+1) are sums
of squares, then (p+q)^(2i+2j+1) is a sum of squares. This is the
published Blekherman–Kozhasov–Reznick theorem, with the truncated-binomial
ingredient credited to Iosif Pinelis. The full credited proof, both source
index/display corrections, arbitrary-degree reduction and edge cases are
included.

## Accepted PARTIAL result

Problem 30000374 / OWR-1116-002 remains unresolved by this work. This edition includes the complete authored proof and full substantive independent internal AI mathematical audit. No mathematical correction was required; the proof is byte-identical to its accepted frozen original.

The result determines the exact empty and singleton Borel degrees. For every countable ordinal α ≥ 2, the related-pair set and a fixed upward section are analytic-complete and non-Borel under the conventional continuous many-one reductions from Baire space, equivalently zero-dimensional Polish source spaces. Color inclusion gives continuous preorder reductions for α ≤ β. For every nonzero α, the least class is the constant zero coloring; the greatest class is characterized by all ordinal tails being dense on one common nonempty interval and has a Σ⁰₃ upper bound. Constant-color and finite-support comparisons are included.

## Exact scope and remaining questions

Set completeness is not analytic preorder universality: the latter requires one Borel map preserving and reflecting all ordered pairs. The exact preorder degrees for α ≥ 2, strictness or reversibility of their inclusion reductions, universality, and mutual-embeddability classification remain unestablished. Rational preservation does not mean surjectivity onto Q. Dense-in-convex-hull witnesses are stronger than embeddings continuous only on the rational subspace. The Σ⁰₃ statement is an upper bound, not a completeness claim.

Question credit: Riccardo Camerlo, “Universal analytic preorders,” Oberwolfach Report 55/2005, printed pp. 3127–3129, Problem 5 on p. 3128.

lambda_k(boundary Omega) |boundary Omega|^(2/m) <= A_m I(Omega)^(1+2/m) + B_m k^(2/m).

## Rigorous partial result, original target unresolved

Adds the complete authored mathematical proof and substantive independent internal audit for problem 30001611 / OWR-4531-003. This is not a counterexample or a universal endpoint cyclicity theorem.

The asymmetric square-root-weight Hilbert model is invertible and bicyclic, with forward norm 1, inverse norm exp(sqrt(n)), and empty adjoint point spectrum. The Banach augmentation-ideal model is invertible and bicyclic, with forward norm 1, inverse logarithmic norm asymptotic to sqrt(n), and adjoint point spectrum exactly the unit circle minus {1}. The spectral condition is noncontainment, not disjointness.

For every 0<a<1/8, explicit bounded functionals annihilate the entire cutoff classes. They prove infinite-dimensional defect quotients and dist_A(z-1,J_A) >= 15/8192. This is a lower bound, not an exact distance. The strict inclusion J_A in I obstructs the subendpoint proof's cutoff-density identification.

Crucially, the Banach defect quotient is cyclic. A proper cutoff ideal and a noncyclic displayed vector do not establish operator noncyclicity. Cyclicity of both full endpoint models remains undetermined by this work; the original problem remains unresolved by this submission.

[Atzmon 1980](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF02392120) is credited for the underlying classical endpoint ideal phenomenon. The [2007 note](https://www.numdam.org/item/10.1016/j.crma.2007.02.008.pdf) and relevant original-report and 1980 portions were inspected. prs.body:
## Prior negative resolution of the unrestricted question

Adds the complete elementary reconstruction and substantive independent internal mathematical audit for problem 30002714 / OWR-13351-013. This is a prior published counterexample, with no new theorem, novelty, or historical-priority claim.

For any field k, start from R = k[x,y,z]_(x,y,z) in K = k(x,y,z), with the explicit rank-three lexicographic valuation v(x) = (0,0,1), v(y) = (0,1,0), v(z) = (1,0,0). The exact local quadratic transforms are R_i = k[x,y/x^i,z/x^i]_(x,y/x^i,z/x^i). Their strict infinite union S is nonarchimedean.

The full proof computes S* = S[1/x] = T = R_(y,z) = k(x)[y,z]_(y,z), including denominator normalization at late stages, the fixed nonzero witness y with yT contained in S, and the elementary UFD complete-closure argument. Neither y/z nor z/y lies in T, so T is not a valuation ring in the original fraction field.

## Accepted partial result: quadratic local-cycle packing

Adds the authored corrected mathematical report, substantive independent internal AI audit, exact source-scope correction, acceptance, and permitted public source metadata for problem 30002668 / OWR-13110-017.

Every general-position arrangement with n red, n blue and n green lines has Omega(n²) pairwise vertex-disjoint properly colored dual four-cycles. General position excludes parallel pairs and triple concurrence. For M differently colored crossings, the exact packing bound is M²/(M + sum_f d(f)²). The planar zone theorem gives sum_f d(f)² <= (C_z+4)N², counting bounded and unbounded faces with their genuine boundary edges. At N=3n and M=3n² this gives at least n²/(C+1/3) disjoint cycles, where C=C_z+4 is absolute.

## Full negative answer at the original index n = 1

Problem 30003045, Question 2 in Ahmed Laghribi's contribution (joint with Roberto Aravire and Manuel O'Ryan) to [Oberwolfach Report 5/2016](https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/46609), asks whether a mixed Kato kernel is always the sum of three individual kernels. This edition gives a full counterexample under the original arbitrary finite purely inseparable hypothesis, at the allowed index n = 1. The original n = 0 equality is proved separately to hold. No failure at every index or every field is claimed.

The base is F_2(b,z,s,t), with beta^4=b, theta^2+theta=s^(-1), and bilinear Pfister form <1,t>_b. The inseparable extension has degree four and exponent two. The form is binary and anisotropic after that extension. The original projective quasilinear-quadric convention includes its zero-dimensional quadric, with function field F(sqrt(t)).

The class represented by s^(-4) b z^2/(1+b z^2) dlog z dies over LK. Restricting a proposed three-summand expression to M=L F(B) kills both the inseparable and Pfister summands. The remaining fixed-slot cyclic algebra would imply a norm. Completion at s forces an impossible residue square-class descent for every possible parameter from F*. The full extra Pfister summand is explicitly included in this exclusion. Choosing the Pfister slot z instead would absorb the class; the independent slot t is essential.

The prior mixed-generator mechanism is credited to Aravire, Laghribi and O'Ryan, [Cohomological kernels of mixed extensions in characteristic 2](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jalgebra.2019.09.012), Journal of Algebra 542 (2020), 249–276. The inspected author manuscript is dated 15 August 2019. The proof does not infer three-summand nonmembership merely from two-field nonsplitting. The exponent-one predecessor is not contradicted. prs.body:
## Full affirmative additive-group result

Every discrete initial ordered additive subgroup of the surreal numbers No is order-group-isomorphic onto an initial subgroup of the omnific integers Oz. The statement covers sets and proper classes in NBG with global choice, including the trivial group. Initiality refers to sign-sequence prefixes. Multiplicative closure and preservation of the original simplicity order are not required. The known discrete initial subdomain theorem is not being substituted for this group result.

The complete proof obtains a minimum exponent -alpha and bottom coefficient group 2^(-n) Z from discreteness. A transfinite sign rotation moves the minimum to zero without creating right-predecessor obligations; scaling the bottom coefficient group gives Z. The canonical Hahn-image characterization then gives initiality, and the Oz normal-form criterion gives containment.

The independent internal AI audit accepts the full stated argument without a mathematical correction. Its complete explicit inverse, all prefix and cross-branch cases, empty tails, arbitrary limit ordinals and successors, canonical Hahn-characterization hypotheses, bottom-unit-monomial normalization, and proper-class bookkeeping are retained. The imported source results are from Philip Ehrlich and Elliot Kaplan, [Number systems with simplicity hierarchies: a generalization of Conway’s theory of surreal numbers II](https://doi.org/10.1017/jsl.2017.9), JSL 83 (2018), 617–633. The target is Question 9.1 in the [authenticated author manuscript](https://elliotakaplan.github.io/Number_systems_with_simplicity_hierarchies_II.pdf) and Question 1 in the Kaplan–Ehrlich contribution to [Oberwolfach Report 60/2016](https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/46663). For problem 30001214 / OWR-3397-002, the unrestricted maximal-spectrum local-closedness assertion is false: in every integer dimension d >= 4, there is a complex affine integral Poisson algebra A and a maximal ideal m whose symplectic core C(m) is not locally closed in Max A.

## Accepted partial result; full single-orbit conjecture unresolved

For problem 30002950, this edition preserves the complete authored partial proof, substantive independent internal AI mathematical/source audit, and algebraic characteristic-transfer supplement for Chen–Viehmann Conjecture 5.1.

With the canonical minimal slope-adapted reference lattice and the stated GL_h minuscule data, every Dieudonne lattice has a unique smallest minimal hull. A cyclic sublattice with the same hull yields the complete colength formula C = sum_i (m_i−1)(n_i−1)/2 + sum_{i<j} m_i n_j, with factors ordered by increasing slope and repeated copies included. If the interior part is nonzero, d(M) <= C and d(M)=C exactly when a(M)=1. Thus the entire a-number-one locus is saturated under invariant-function strata and their J-orbits.

The proof and supplement cover W(k) and k[[t]] with q-Frobenius. They retain bounded exponent differences in annihilator division, epsilon-adic convergence, Witt carries, cross-slope corrections and finite-field independence for repeated slopes. A nonbasic isocrystal with one interior slope plus ordinary factors reduces to the published basic theorem. The entirely ordinary empty locus is treated separately. The exact rank-six gluing example prevents an unjustified interior slopewise direct-sum argument.

The full single J-orbit assertion when there are multiple distinct interior slopes remains unresolved. Hull and colength do not determine the full invariant function. Sampled J-profiles and finite controls are not a universal orbit proof. The full conjecture is neither proved nor disproved, and no novelty is claimed.

prs.body:
## Accepted partial result; exact target unresolved

Problem 30001551 / OWR-4425-006 asks whether exactly three independent constant-free equations on three variables, with nonempty variable words on both sides, admit one common nonperiodic solution in a finite-alphabet free monoid. Empty variable images are allowed; independence concerns the complete solution set.

This unrefereed AI-assisted exposition and independent internal AI mathematical/source/computational audit accept three partial statements:

- At most one equation of a hypothetical independent triple with a common nonperiodic solution admits an erasing deletion witness.
- If the triple has a common erasing nonperiodic solution, no equation admits an erasing deletion witness.
- A balanced three-variable system with a common nonperiodic solution and a member equivalent to pairwise commutation is equivalent to at most two original members.

The complete proof and substantive audit are preserved. The exact supplied clarification patch is applied: the two-word criterion uses injectivity of an indexed morphism on distinct formal letters, correctly covering equal and empty images; the three-profile heading explicitly concerns nonperiodic erasing morphisms. No theorem, hypothesis, or inference changes.

The erasure mechanism is credited to Holub–Žemlička, [Algebraic properties of word equations](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jalgebra.2015.03.021), Lemmas 15–16. The balanced reduction uses Saarela, [On the Solution Sets of Three-Variable Word Equations](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00224-024-10193-9), Lemma 4.4. Nowotka–Saarela's [2022 bound](https://doi.org/10.1137/20M1310448) is 17 with a common nonperiodic solution; 18 concerns systems without that requirement. No novelty or improved general bound is claimed.

Both bounded searches were reconstructed independently with exact arithmetic and every signature bit compared: 157,800 equations / 216 binary morphisms / 5 signatures / 10 triples, and 28,216 equations / 2,744 binary morphisms / 15 signatures / 455 triples. No triple passes on either finite pool. This does not rule out longer or nonbinary witnesses at the searched equation lengths, longer equations, or systems whose common nonperiodic solutions are all nonerasing. It does not exclude erasing common nonperiodic solutions. The exact target remains unresolved by this work.

The complete authored proof constructs a finite two-dimensional simplicial complex K that is doubly Cohen–Macaulay over Q, and hence over every characteristic-zero field, but contains no two-dimensional homology-sphere subcomplex over any field. Homology sphere includes all face-link conditions. Thus Nevo's homology-sphere-cover question has a negative answer before its overlap and reordering requirements arise.

prs.body:
## Accepted theorem; combined target only partially resolved

For problem 30003650, this edition preserves the complete proof of p_n^+=p_n for every n>=1, including singular matrices with finite strictly positive factorizations. It also proves P_(n,r)^+=P_(n,r) on every exact ordinary-matrix-rank stratum 1<=r<=n. Both maxima are attained. The convention is A=BB^T with an n by p factor B; every entry of a positive factor is strictly positive.

The combined two-question target is ACCEPT_AS_PARTIAL. Its maximum-gap question g_n=max(cp^+(A)-cp(A)) remains undetermined in general. The result does not supply explicit ordinary maxima p_n in every order, and does not assert equality of the two ranks for every individual matrix. No novelty is claimed.

The self-contained proof uses finite conic reduction, closedness of bounded ordinary-CP-rank sets by a trace-bounded factor argument, and two invertible congruences. Positive congruence gives attained positive-factor witnesses without decreasing the ordinary CP-rank for sufficiently small parameters. Negative congruence preserves a given positive factor on the explicit interval 0<t<=alpha/2, and its strictly positive inverse pulls a minimal nonnegative factor back to a positive factor. Removing zero columns is essential. Both congruences preserve ordinary rank, with no extension of an ambient-interior theorem to singular boundary points.

The retained bounds are g_1=g_2=g_3=0, 0<=g_4<=1 and 1<=g_n<=p_n-3 for n>=5. Low-order equality and gap-one witnesses are attributed to Bomze–Dickinson–Still. The rank-r bound is P_(n,r)-r; the positive-definite bound p_n-n is not claimed for all singular matrices. Row duplication shows g_n is nondecreasing but does not determine it.

For Karpenkov's historical eight-sail Klein model, this unrefereed AI-assisted manuscript proves countably infinitely many GL(3,Z)-inequivalent continued fractions in every fixed totally real cubic field. - The actual eight-sail union recovers the defining hyperplanes, their rational multiplication algebra, and an integral multiplier order. The recovered-order trace discriminant is geometric and must not be confused with an operator-polynomial discriminant.
- The lattices Z + f O_K have invariant f⁴ disc(K), proving pairwise inequivalence for all positive integers f. Every full lattice has an irreducible positive-eigenvalue SL(3,Z) realization.
- The exact lattice criterion is J = a tau(I), for a nonzero field scalar and a genuine field automorphism. It includes all full lattices and orders, without assuming invertibility over a nonmaximal order.

prs.body:
## Accepted partial theorem; unrestricted singleton problem unresolved

For strictly increasing positive integer moduli n_i, one canonical forbidden residue 0 <= a_i < n_i, and inclusive activation m >= n_i, the survivor set has logarithmic density whenever, outside a reciprocal-summable exceptional family, the residues satisfy one of finitely many fixed identities q a_i = p n_i + c with integer q >= 1, p, c. The density equals the decreasing limit of the finite-periodic survivor densities. Coprimality, disjointness, bounded residues, and reciprocal summability of the patterned family are unnecessary. Natural density of the infinite survivor set is not asserted.

In the fully patterned class, arbitrary finite positive per-modulus activation thresholds preserve this logarithmic density. The summable exceptional family retains the original activation condition. The audit's explicit counterexample rejects extending threshold invariance to arbitrary summable exceptions; it is not a counterexample to the theorem or to the unrestricted original target.

PROOF.md is the complete accepted proof, preserved verbatim: 15,022 bytes, SHA-256 bd97cb7fdf168742d082866c553f48705c571b90895011087031ad3fa7710174. It contains the primitive-set lemma, restricted-multiple valuation strata and tail bound, affine pullback, cutoff-chain argument, exceptional-family bound, threshold corollary, and odd-composite example. The substantive audit is retained in full, with privacy and explicit review-scope editorial changes only. No mandatory mathematical corrections were found. The optional shorter cutoff argument is retained in the audit but not substituted into the proof.

The proof uses [Davenport–Erdős (1936)](https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1936-04.pdf), Theorem 1(a) together with the finite-union constant, at its stated strength. The original singleton formulation comes from [Erdős (1995), section I.4](https://www.ime.usp.br/~yoshi/resenhas/abstracts/Erdos.pdf). [Araújo's dissertation](https://digital.ub.uni-paderborn.de/hs/download/pdf/8306542) supplies summability background. The [Chojecki manuscript](https://www.ulam.ai/research/erdos25.pdf) remains partial/conditional, and the [proposed Wang multiple-residue result](https://multiscalar.ai/results/erdos-486/) expressly excludes the singleton conclusion; neither proposed program is imported as a proof dependency.

## Accepted partial theorem; factorial-minus-one irrationality unresolved

Let H_N = sum_{n=2}^N 1/(n!-1), let Q_N be its positive reduced denominator, and let S be the infinite sum. The complete elementary proof establishes:

1. limsup log(Q_N)/(N^(3/2) log N) >= 1/3.
2. For every fixed 0 < c < 1/3, the set A_c = {N >= 2: log Q_N >= c N^(3/2) log N} has lower asymptotic density at least 1/2.
3. Q_N(S-H_N) tends to positive infinity through A_c.

This is a reduced-denominator result, not merely an unreduced-lcm bound. It rests on the reciprocal-sum cancellation lemma P | D G^2, a factorial-gap estimate, exact terminal-block/prefix divisibility, the asymptotic constant, and residue-class chains in fourth-power intervals. For A contained in (1,infinity), suppose |kx-y| >= 1 for every ordered pair of distinct elements and every positive integer k. Then H_A(X) = sum_{x in A, x <= X} 1/x = o(log X), and consequently sum_{x in A, x < n} 1/x = o(log n) along integers.

orientations and, by the correspondence as presented by Benson, Chakrabarty
and Tetali, maximal parking functions. The complete substantive proof and

## Corrected partial results; general two-set question unresolved

For every 3-permutable set S and every fixed integer C >= 0, only finitely many positive integers n have the whole integer interval [n,2n-C] contained in S. The complete proof gives the equivalent divergent-deficit conclusion, the P >= k+2 finite-prefix bound for k distinct C3 scales and two fixed anchors, and the stated bounded-additive-dyadic-run and monochromatic-interval exclusions.

## Scoped prior result and endpoint audit

For Ball 2002 Problem 4 / 2000004 / AMR-019-0004, this draft credits the Almi–Krömer–Molchanova Lavrentiev-gap result in its exact two-component Ciarlet–Nečas setting. The accepted ranges are d=2 with p>2 and 1<q<p/(p−2), and d=3 with 3<p<4 and 2<q<p/(p−2). The homogeneous polyconvex energy forces continuity; both comparison classes have the same partial Dirichlet data and CN constraint.

The prior source is [A new example for the Lavrentiev phenomenon in nonlinear elasticity](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00033-023-02132-4), ZAMP 75, article 2 (2024). The inspected versions are the publisher PDF and [arXiv:2309.08288v2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.08288v2), revised 8 November 2023. Existence, finite-distortion, change-of-variables and topological results remain external cited dependencies; their deep proofs were not independently reconstructed.

### Two-dimensional endpoint qualification

The logarithmic competitor printed after (3.9) in arXiv pages 10–11 and publisher page 9 has infinite inverse-Jacobian energy at q=p/(p−2). The exact lower-triangular determinant is J=A t^(alpha+beta−1)(alpha L+1)/L^4. At the endpoint it gives J^(−q) comparable above and below to t^(−1)L^(3q), whose reference-coordinate integral diverges. Both printed logarithmic denominator powers are preserved. This is a failed construction/proof step, not a disproof of the endpoint theorem. The strict-range 2D and 3D arguments do not use that endpoint construction.

The complete authored theorem summary, source/hypothesis audit, endpoint/proof notes and bounded acceptance are retained. The proof notes include the normalized distortion term W(I)|Omega_s| and the integrated positive-part/Hölder repair with coefficient 2^(1−p). Two precision edits say that the gradient is lower triangular and that the slice excess quantity is the integral of D(x_1)^p.

No unqualified solution to Ball's connected-domain, boundary-only formulation, no everywhere-injective homeomorphism-class result, and no novelty are claimed. Remark 3.1 does not supply the missing connector estimates or preserve boundary-only constraints by itself. The bounded correction search on 10 October 2026 found no repair; it was not exhaustive. No author was contacted.

## Accepted partial analytic result; irrationality remains unresolved

For every fixed finite set of at least two distinct primes, the complete proof establishes a moving-phase leading asymptotic for the actual repeated running-LCM tails. Every positive smooth integer, including 1, contributes; repeated denominators are retained. The strict-prefix normalization is P_a/p, where p is the least prime, and the leading scale is a^(|P|-1).

On each fixed arithmetic progression, the normalized subsequential limit set contains a nondegenerate interval of positive values. This is not a claim that the entire limit set is one interval, and it assumes no rational independence of reciprocal prime logarithms. The closed-cube continuity, multiplicative face identities and compact-subgroup loop argument are fully proved.

No fixed finite family of real polynomial corrections can give a little-o leading-scale remainder, even with arbitrary indexwise choice. Fixed-period quasipolynomials are excluded in particular. For {2,3,5}, the progression oscillation constant is certified strictly between 0.0127214469683 and 0.0127214469684, and the limsup/liminf ratio is at least 5/3. ## Variable-base universal extension refuted; fixed base 2 unresolved

This prose-only edition retains the complete substantive proof and independent
mathematical audit. No mathematical correction was required. The combined

Let P(X)=X^4-X^3-X^2-X-1, let gamma be its unique positive root, and define
c=1/((gamma-1)P'(gamma)), alpha=2c gamma^20, and beta=gamma alpha.
Then 1.92<gamma<1.93 and alpha/beta=1/gamma is irrational. Every indexed
term floor(alpha gamma^n) and floor(beta gamma^n), for n>=0, is even.
Every positive odd integer is omitted from finite sums of distinct positions.
Equal values at different positions remain usable separately and cannot
remove this parity obstruction.

The explicit trace recurrence has residue 1/3. Exact root/coefficient bounds
imply |E_m|<3(5/6)^m<1/6 for every m>=20, giving strict floor endpoints.
The shift 20 covers both exponent-zero terms. The historical independent
check also isolates the unshifted m=3 floor as the odd integer 1, emphasizing
why an unproved eventual-to-all-positions step would be invalid.

The original hypotheses permit beta=gamma alpha for irrational gamma.
At gamma=2 the corresponding ratio is rational and inadmissible. Therefore
this counterexample addresses the universal extension to 1<gamma<2;
it does not resolve the original fixed-base-2 question or classify all bases.

with F(n)-n<=K have natural density zero. Thus F(n)-n tends to infinity in
natural density. Neither eventual positivity for all sufficiently large n
nor pointwise divergence is established. A density-zero set is not proved
finite, and no global last exception is claimed.

The self-contained proof derives Var(S)<=Hv for reduced-residue counts modulo
even squarefree Q directly from CRT joint probabilities, nonnegative divisor
expansion, a triangular-sum bound, and exact Euler-product cancellation.
It neither assumes independence nor requires H<Q. Elementary product bounds
and prime density zero give the composite-witness transfer. The density limit
is taken with H and Q fixed; only afterward is H enlarged.

obstruction at primorial multiples, endpoint/parity reductions, the correct
square-root upper bound, the exact prime-square identities

counterexample to either original universal target.

## Accepted partial theorem; exact asymptotic unresolved

For the classical Hofstadter consecutive-sum sequence with seed (1,2), each
later term is the least integer strictly greater than its predecessor that is
a sum of at least two consecutive earlier terms. The accepted theorem gives,
for every integer n>=2, with all logarithms natural,

    a_n-n >= (log(log(n))-log(log(5)+log(2)/3))/log(4).

The finite plateau lemma gives V<Q<=2*T^2*(T-1)^2<2*T^4 for any
constant-deviation interval 3<=r<=s, where T=a_r, V=a_s and Q is the least
2*4^k strictly above T^2*(T-1)^2/2. This subfamily of powers makes 8Q a square;
the positive one-sided crossing error is excluded by a difference of squares.
The all-index threshold recurrence handles skipped levels and nonempty
plateaus and starts at M(0)=5. No mathematical correction was required.

The result improves the specific log20 coefficient displayed in Theorem 1.4
of [Quanyu Tang, The Hofstadter consecutive-sum sequence omits infinitely
many positive integers, arXiv:2603.09939v2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.09939v2),
revised 23 March 2026. Tang's plateau and threshold-function strategy is
credited explicitly. The prior polynomial upper bounds are recorded with
attribution and are not independently re-proved here. Public metadata describes

prs.body:
## Accepted corrected prior theorem; coefficient one unresolved

For one absolute C>0 and infinitely many positive integers n, the complete
corrected proof establishes

    omega(n-k) <= Omega(n-k) <= C log k,  for every integer 2<=k<n.

Here omega counts distinct factors, Omega counts with multiplicity, and log
is natural. Credit is given to Cheuk Fung (Joshua) Lau, *On the Number of
Prime Factors of Consecutive Integers*, [arXiv:2604.15042v2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.15042v2),
24 June 2026, Theorem 1.3. This is an authored proof correction and audit of
that prior result, with no novelty or whole-problem resolution claim.

With N=n-1 and epsilon=1/(C log 2), every positive integer m<N satisfies
m+epsilon*Omega(m)<=N, hence m+epsilon*omega(m)<=N, for infinitely many N.
The same one positive epsilon works throughout. The closest endpoint uses
k=2, not the excluded k=1. No explicit numerical C or epsilon is certified.
The original distinct-prime weak-inequality formulation was checked in
[Erdos, Some unconventional problems in number theory, Acta 33 (1979),
printed p.71](https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1979-23.pdf).

Coefficient one remains unresolved. The logarithmic result controls it only
beyond a fixed cutoff, leaving a finite terminal window of simultaneous
inequalities at infinitely many witnesses. The epsilon transfer does not
eliminate that obligation for coefficient one.

## Complete proof corrections and independent acceptance

The primary proof modules are preserved byte-for-byte:
KERNEL_REPAIR.md, DISTINCT_OMEGA_RECONSTRUCTION.md and MULTIPLICITY_REPAIR.md.

correction, valid integrated normalization, restricted distinct-prime moments,

With full prime valuations and the strict p<t boundary, f(n,t) counts distinct

integer N. Hence any universal coefficient in f(n,t)>=ct satisfies

example was independently reproduced; no minimum at t=500 or best-in-literature
claim follows. A positive uniform lower coefficient remains unresolved.

with the gcd-label partition modulo M_t=product_{p<t}q_p, with q_p the least
p-power at least t. The earlier report already contains this finite-period
reduction and is credited. Singleton numerical labels need not be periodic.

The safe-lift normal form is exact for the global minimum. Replacing an unsafe
lift by a safe one changes only a singleton gcd label, so cannot increase the
number of classes. For h=q_p/p, the retained count is
K_p(t)=h+(p-1)*max(0,t-(p-1)*h)<=t. At most t^pi(t-1) CRT tuples suffice.

novelty, priority or optimality assertion is made.

## Accepted prior fixed-r matching order

The prior STARFLEET Math result for Erdős Problem 538 is accepted as a
conventional mathematical proof. For every fixed integer r>=2,

    E_r(N)=Theta_r(log N/log log N).

E_r(N) maximizes S(A)=sum_{a in A}1/a over positive a<=N, with at most r
ordered pairs (p,a), p prime, a in A, m=pa, for every integer m.
The cap includes products above N. Arbitrary admissible sets need not be
squarefree; squarefreeness is used only in the constructed lower witnesses.
This is an audit of a prior public claim, credited to STARFLEET Math, with
no novelty claim.

The accepted finite inequalities are

    log(log(N+1)) S(A) <= 2r(1+log(N^2)), for r>=2 and N>=2,
    log(N+1) <= 4+8192(ell(N)+1) S(A_N), for every natural N,

where A_N has global cap two. Put L(0)=0, L(N)=floor(log_2 N) for N>=1,
and ell(N)=floor(log_2 L(N)) when L(N)>=1, otherwise ell(N)=0.
All unsubscripted logarithms are natural. No real logarithm of zero occurs.

for prime q and k>x/q, every edge preserves the q-rough part R_q(k).
Division by a fixed rough part d yields precisely the smooth fiber with left
cutoff s>floor(x/d)/q and upper endpoint floor(n/d), and right interval
(floor(n/d),floor(x/d)]. Prime factors in the smooth part are strictly below q.

graph has no matching. E(16)=40, equivalently H(16)=24. This disproves exact
sufficiency of the specified full smoothness/size-tail tests, even including

## Attributed prior bounds; uniform exponent-one upper question unresolved

This prose-only edition preserves the complete authored derivations and acceptance of three prior works on distinct multiples in intervals. Define f(n,m) as the least length H for which (m,m+H] contains distinct multiples of 1,...,n; F(n)=max_m f(n,m); h_P(n) is the prime-only maximum. All logarithms are natural.

- Wouter van Doorn's published theorem gives F(n)-f(n,n)>0.36 n log n/log log n eventually.
- Scott Duke Kominers's arXiv:2607.10431v1 gives liminf [F(n)-f(n,n)]/(n log n)>=1/e.
- Kaizhe Chen and Samuel Korsky's arXiv:2607.26450v2 gives F(n)<=n^(4/3) exp(O(log n/log log n)), h_P(n)<<n^(4/3)/(log n)^(1/3), and F(n)>=h_P(n)>=n exp(((log 2)/2-o(1))log n/log log n).

The last lower bound and the known diagonal upper estimate imply [F(n)-f(n,n)]/(n log n)->infinity. This is a consequence of the credited prior results, not a new theorem. The uniform upper question F(n)<=n^(1+o(1)) remains unresolved by these results. The fixed-start asymptotic in Erdos Problem 710 is separate and is not settled here. A 4/3 upper exponent does not approach 1.

## Complete authored argument and exact scope

The accepted original audit is 21,040 bytes, SHA-256 43c210e38a0dc03080c955812c025cd269a260855a793a56f972f3195b8670f5. ## Accepted restricted-family result

The full EP-509 question remains unresolved. This edition preserves the complete
authored written proofs and independent audit, with no required mathematical
correction and no claim of novelty, priority, an improved general bound, or a
solution of the unrestricted disk-cover problem. The alias is 2304007 /
AMR-022-4007, Hayman's Problem 4.7.

For every compact planar set with finitely many connected components, the
finite/countable closed-disk covering content equals the minimum sum of
circumradii over partitions of those components. The minimum is attained.
Thus a fixed polynomial's bounds 2+epsilon for every epsilon>0 would imply

every k<=d<=256. The starting point has no upper cutoff. The inclusive
disjoint boundary d=k and all prime-power exponents are included.

## Accepted prior original-statement result

The prior EP730 proof is accepted as a conventional mathematical solution:
infinitely many distinct positive n<m have equal prime supports of
binomial(2n,n) and binomial(2m,m). Infinitely many consecutive pairs occur.
This is an audit of prior work, with no new-solution or novelty claim.

As credited by the author's public formalization manifest, Liam Price
provided the informal idea, Tomodovodoo an algebraic follow-up, and Will Blair
the analytic reconstruction/formalization. The author describes review as
self-assessed and the earlier informal argument as unadjudicated. Priority
and unavailable antecedent material were not independently authenticated.

With T=5289, P=42Tx+11, Q=72Tx+13, R=28Tx+5 and S=72Tx+19, the family is

    n(x)=P(x)Q(x)−1=84591927504x²+7076682x+142.

The lower asymptotic density of successful positive parameters x is strictly
greater than 107/2500. This is density in x, not in n or in all pairs. The
positive strictly increasing quadratic makes x -> (n(x),n(x)+1) injective
and completes the original-statement bridge. Equality of prime supports is
not equality of valuations or of central binomial coefficients.

## Accepted conditional partial result

For an ordinary real-valued additive function f with density-zero strict
decreases, suppose that for one fixed real c the residual f−c log is
approximable by periodic sequences in density. Then f(n)=c log n for every
positive integer, with c≥0. A sufficient condition is
Σ_p min(1,|f(p)−c log p|)/p<∞. Values at higher prime powers may be arbitrary
finite real numbers; complete additivity is not assumed.

The complete written proof uses a bounded arctangent transform, vanishing
mean variation, fixed-period averaging without a period-dependent loss,
tightness excluding either endpoint, and fixed coprime-dilation witnesses.
The prime-tail argument treats large-prime squares and finite-small-prime
valuation truncation separately, with the order of limits explicit.
Two lifting lemmas and all mathematical boundary examples are retained.
Absolute o(1) logarithmic approximation off o(X) exceptions already suffices,
even when its slope and offset vary with X, because the offset cancels.

The unrestricted EP 1122 / 2503 problem remains unresolved by this work.
Density-zero decreases alone have not been shown to imply the periodic
residual premise, the sufficient prime-tail condition, or absolute
vanishing-error approximation. No unrestricted counterexample, novelty,
priority, or exhaustive current literature-status claim is made.

## Full proofs and independent audit

The original mathematical Sections 1–4 are retained verbatim in PROOF.md,
and the independent reconstruction in mathematical Sections 2–6 is retained
verbatim in AUDIT.md. No mathematical correction was required. The written
proofs are self-contained; no computational premise or external analytic
theorem is omitted. Boundary examples include a bounded parity defect,
isolated exact-valuation defects with positive decrease density, a slowly
varying divergent scalar slope, and the arctangent endpoint obstruction.
None is a counterexample to the unrestricted density-zero problem.

Historical independent supporting checks include 729 exact rational variation
tests, 1,364 period-average contractions, 16,388 finite bad-set dilation
checks, 555 ordinary-additive coprime-pair checks with arbitrary prime-power
values, 512 valuation-truncation checks, and 27 finite tail/Markov checks.

weighted bidirected tree is included. A bidirected triangle is excluded by

integer firing-bound vector, not a claimed reachable endpoint. The
nonhalting certificate is a nonnegative integrally equivalent configuration
and a legal once-per-vertex recurrent sequence. Signed least action,
Eulerian equivalence shifts, block-potential telescoping, both decision
directions, class recognition, O(n²) arithmetic counts, polynomial bit
bounds, and the literal degree-zero singleton convention are retained.

terminating-play family are proved analytically.

## Accepted restricted result

This authored prose edition proves a sufficient fixed-rank-block criterion
for simultaneous lower and upper matroid degree bounds. For block
incidence κ, one basis satisfies both sides within additive κ−1 and costs
at most L. When κ≤Δ, this gives the requested additive Δ−1 on the stated
restricted class. The same-basis complement reduction is proved fully.

L is the LP optimum AFTER ceiling/floor normalization of rational degree
bounds, not the weaker unrounded rational-bound LP. Original integral
feasibility gives L≤OPT. Finite rational costs can be negative.

Canonical exchange components are the finest fixed-rank blocks and are
pointwise incidence-minimal only in the stated indexed anchor-complement
model retaining every original upper row. This does not exclude pruning,
merging duplicates, linear combinations, face restriction, or other methods.

The tight-face extension uses a direct sum of successive matroid minors.
It returns an original basis costing at most a specified feasible LP point.
For a chosen optimal point with face incidence at most Δ, the desired
restricted guarantee follows. The complete polynomial tight-set preorder
and maximal-chain construction are included. There is no guarantee of
finding a favorable point by searching all LP optima.

## Complete proof and accepted dependencies

The complete upper-only Király–Lau–Singh argument is reproduced with
attribution, including the equality-case linear dependence and the
selected-cost-plus-residual-optimum invariant for negative costs. It needs
LP feasibility, not an exactly degree-feasible integral basis.

Standard polynomial submodular minimization, rank-polytope separation,
and rational LP optimization/basic-optimum extraction are accepted oracle
dependencies. They are neither re-proved nor implemented by this edition.
The general proofs are complete subject to those stated standard tools.
No substantive proof correction was required by the independent audit.

## Historical finite evidence and reproduction limit

The graphic K5 example was separately checked to show that a face can
satisfy the criterion when the original matroid does not. The KLS example
was separately checked as a stalled elementary-rounding instance with a
unique fractional optimum. A checked relaxed-basis convex decomposition
shows cost-preserving existence relative to that point for every linear
objective. The stalled vertex does not refute the target guarantee.

The independent historical audit checked all 125 graphic bases, all 64
specified face bases, all 1,024 graphic rank subsets, all 96 KLS bases,
and all 4,096 KLS rank subsets. Additional controls covered normalization,
LP-only feasibility, negative costs, equality dependence, and boundary
coordinates. Normal, -O, and -OO runs passed, including 36 negative and
6 positive controls. Candidate programs were not imported or executed
by the independent audit.

Numerical instance definitions, coordinates, explicit finite witness and
basis lists, matrices, detailed tables, raw certificates, executable code,
and copied source documents are omitted. The omitted augmented exemplars
are not self-contained or computationally reproducible from this edition
alone. They are supporting evidence, not premises of the general theorems.
Preparation performed editorial and byte-integrity checks only, without
new mathematical executions or scholarly-source inspection.

## Sources, status, and remaining question

Tamás Király, Lap Chi Lau, and Mohit Singh,
[*Degree Bounded Matroids and Submodular Flows*](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00493-012-2760-6),
Combinatorica 32(6), 703–720 (2012), supplies the established upper-only
rounding result and Remark 1 obstruction. Public author PDF:
https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/~lapchi/papers/submodular.pdf .

Kristóf Bérczi, André Berger, Matthias Mnich, and Roland Vincze,
[*Degree-Bounded Generalized Polymatroids and Approximating the Metric Many-Visits TSP*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.09890v2),
provides related two-sided 2Δ−1 and one-sided Δ−1 context. Egres Open's
[*Bounded degree matroid basis*](https://oldlemon.cs.elte.hu/egres/open/Bounded_degree_matroid_basis)
is the retained target formulation, not current-status certification.

by this work when the criterion fails. No novelty, priority, exhaustive
literature survey, hardness theorem, or general counterexample is claimed.

separating-sphere twist is detected by a knot in that category. Knots may
be unoriented embedded circles; no framing or prime-summand restriction

## Accepted prior construction, with ancillary corrections

This authored edition independently reconstructs the core of Theorem 1 in
M. Czech's pinned July 2026 manuscript. Every positive integral solution of
z²−56x²=65 with x≥37 gives five explicit distinct divisors of
n=(x²−1)(x²−4)(x²−16)(x²−49) in the strictly open right interval
(√n,√n+31 n^(1/4)). A positive Pell recurrence from (37,277) yields
infinitely many distinct n. Any K in the original one-sided uniform-bound
formulation therefore satisfies K≥5. The general EP887 question remains
unresolved by this work.

This is an audit of a prior construction, not a newly claimed theorem.
The complete elementary factorization, positivity, distinctness, strict
window inequalities, finite base cases and infinitude proof are retained.
No external upper-bound theorem, general Pell existence theorem, complete
divisor census, or author-supplied verifier is a proof dependency.

## Corrections and limits

- 31 is the least integer constant for all five displayed divisors at every
  admissible parameter. It is not least among real constants: 30.5 works
  throughout the family. Every C>30 works eventually; C≤30 never contains
  all five displayed divisors. The shifted-polynomial proof and all 26
  small-parameter square exclusions are public.
- Pell necessity applies only to the fifth pair with its prescribed midpoint.
  An explicit off-Pell additional-divisor witness is retained without making
  a complete-census claim.
- The original question is one-sided; a symmetric version changes the
  numerical normalization and is not a general same-window count equality.
- The balanced-split method is shared with the consecutive-factor construction;
  the weight sets are not literal affine recenterings. Exhaustive maximality
  is not asserted from an omitted enumeration.

The nonsquareness argument is retained. Complete sample counts, eventual
exact-five behavior, the incomplete secondary family, speculative sixth-pair
and geometric exclusions, and historical priority or record claims are
outside this edition's accepted conclusions.

  refinement of the Erdős–Rosenfeld construction](https://czechu.blog/erdos/problems/887/note887.pdf),

  construction; the printed Proposition 4.1 interval typo is not silently repaired.
- Chan, [arXiv:1303.2069v1](https://arxiv.org/abs/1303.2069v1): a
  sufficiently-large-square result, with the central root counted in the

  almost-square result whose plus sign and small-factor-offset hypothesis
  are essential. Entire cited upper-bound proof chains are not independently

## Accepted restricted result

This authored prose edition proves simultaneous proportional edge
factorization for every finite loopless bipartite multigraph whose connected
components each have empty or regular nonempty 2-core. For arbitrary
positive real fractions summing to one, the same partition satisfies every
color's floor/ceiling quota at every original vertex degree. Core degrees
may vary between components, and arbitrary finite trees may be attached.
Parallel edges, forests, bipartite pseudoforests, isolated vertices, the null
graph, and one color are covered. Irregular surviving 2-cores are outside
the sufficient hypothesis. No mathematical correction was required.

## Complete general proofs

The finite quota-word lemma includes its lower-bound circulation reduction
and integral augmenting-flow proof; it uses the original real fractions.
The complete multiplicity-aware core-structure argument and alternating-path
proof of the perfect-matching decomposition are retained. Monotone prefix
counts extend core colors to attachment edges, and one-precolored-edge
completion propagates through trees. Quotas use original degrees throughout.

The fixed-instance rational-cell lemma preserves both integer threshold
equalities and strict inequalities, including zero-degree and zero/one
unfixed-coordinate cases. It gives no bounded-denominator testing guarantee.
The main theorem treats arbitrary real fractions directly and uses no
finite computation as a premise.

## Authored obstructions and omitted finite premises

A historically checked ten-vertex tree shows that an arbitrary valid first
proportional factor need not extend, even with unrestricted choice of the
remaining colors. The authored local forcing contradiction and its real
parameter region are retained. A historically checked six-cycle point
shows a fractional vertex and non-total-unimodularity of the natural
joint-color LP. The authored odd-cycle determinant and tight-rank arguments
are retained. Both underlying graphs have full valid partitions; neither
obstruction refutes the target.

Explicit graph/factor and coordinate witness packages, indexed rows and
columns, raw matrix certificates, executable code, and raw certificates are
omitted. Realization of each obstruction's stated finite premises is a
historical checked fact, not a self-contained reconstruction in this prose
edition. The general theorem and rational-cell lemma are complete and do
not depend on either obstruction. This is not a computational reproduction
package.

## Historical checks and stream-hash qualification

The independent historical audit checked 15,674 in-scope K3,3 partitions,
4,323 labeled-tree partitions, six retained concrete partitions, both
obstructions, and multiplicity, exact irrational, rational-cell boundary,
endpoint, and negative controls. Normal, -O, and -OO receipts agree.
Candidate programs were not used as implementation source, imported, or
executed by the independent audit.

The candidate's unretained full generated stream hash is authenticated
author-reported metadata only. The audit constructed its own valid
partitions; it did not recreate that stream and claims no byte-identical
reproduction. Edition preparation performed editorial and byte-integrity
checks only, with no new mathematical run or scholarly-source inspection.

## Sources and status

J. R. Correa and M. X. Goemans,
[*Improved bounds on nonblocking 3-stage Clos networks*](https://doi.org/10.1137/060656413),
SIAM Journal on Computing 37(3), 870–894 (2007), Section 2, supplies
two-factor and relaxed-decomposition context. Public author PDF:
https://www.dii.uchile.cl/~jcorrea/papers/Journals/CG2007.pdf .

[*Edge Coloring and Decompositions of Weighted Graphs*](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-540-87744-8_34),

Theorem 1.5, and Sections 1.1–1.2 and 3, records the target and contextual
bounds. Public research-site PDF:
https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/wp-content/uploads/2008/09/edgecoloring.pdf .

The retained Egres Open revision 2419,
[*Partitioning a bipartite graph into proportional factors*](https://oldlemon.cs.elte.hu/egres/open/Partitioning_a_bipartite_graph_into_proportional_factors),
is the target formulation, not a current-status certification. The audit's
